newsitem.title: MOZAMBIQUE: World Bank chief praises Mozambique.
newsitem.headline: World Bank chief praises Mozambique.

text.p: World Bank President James Wolfensohn ended a two-day visit to Mozambique on Sunday with praise for the southern African country's "remarkable progress" towards increased economic growth.
Wolfensohn told a news conference at Maputo's airport the World Bank was prepared to strengthen its support for the government's programme to achieve even faster economic growth.

"I and my colleagues at the Bank want to deepen our partnership with Mozambique and broaden our consultation with the government, the private sector, non-governmental organisations and the other development partners," he said.
Wolfensohn said he was impressed by its "remarkable progress through a peaceful transition to to democracy and on to increased economic stability and growth."
Wolfensohn said the decline in Mozambique's inflation rate was helping the poor, while financial sector reforms were paving the way for new industries and jobs.
During his stay in Mozambique, Wolfensohn met President Joaquim Chissano, Prime Minister Pascoal Mocumbi, other members of government, representatives of the private sectors and academics.
He also attended a meeting during which the transport ministers of Mozambique and South Africa, Paulo Muxanga and Mac Maharaj, made a joint presentation on the Maputo Development Corridor.

It was the first time that Motambique, South Africa and the World Bank had come together to discuss this regional development initiative. Wolfensohn said the World Bank would give the corridor project its full support.
Last year the World Bank approved $2.7 billion in loans for African countries covering 53 projects. Wolfensohn was on a nine-day Africa trip which included stops in Senegal, Ghana and South Africa.
